subject: StrataCore peaking sensitivity + reserve sizing proposal
messages:
From: Linda Chen <linda.chen@stratacore.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Dec 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fleet peaking profile + capacity ask for P1 launch

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for taking a look. We attached our Q4->Q1 traffic forecast (daily and 5-min peaks). High-level:
- Expected steady-state conversation traffic: ~18M tokens/day (avg prompt+completion ~600 tokens).
- Expected daily embedding batch jobs: ~10M embedding vectors (short inputs, heavy batch windows at 02:00 UTC).
- Peak 5-min token surge estimate (marketing campaign): ~14k concurrent tokens/sec sustained for ~14 mins.

SLOs: p95 generation latency <= 400ms for the primary chat endpoint; embedding throughput required to finish nightly batch in a 2h window.

Questions we need answered for procurement:
1) Recommended committed slab (tokens/sec) to meet SLO with 20% safety margin.
2) Burst policy: how much burst above commit can we rely on, and fallback behavior if exceeded.
3) If we use 4-bit quantization for chat models, any notable latency tradeoffs you expect under heavy peaking.

I've attached the forecast. Can you share a sizing that maps tokens/sec -> GPU slab counts and expected p95 latency at target concurrency? Procurement wants numbers for their SOW.

[Attachment: stratacore_forecast_q4-q1.xlsx (Excel, 95KB)]

Thanks,
Linda
Product Ops | StrataCore

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Chen <linda.chen@stratacore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Dec 2027 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet peaking profile + capacity ask for P1 launch

Linda —

Thanks for the forecast, that helped. I ran a conservative pass against our dedicated-slab model and attached the capacity workbook ("redwood_stratacore_capacity_model_v2.xlsx"). High-level recommendation up front so procurement can proceed:

- Committed slab: 6 x rtx-c24-equivalent GPUs (dedicated slab) configured for chat model (gptx-13b-v2) with 12x batching and hot KV cache.
- Committed tokens/sec (effective, steady-state): 9,500 tps (this maps to your steady-state + 20% safety).
- Burst allowance: automatic burst to 12,000 tps for up to 20 minutes per hour under our priority queuing; beyond that, graceful fallback to smaller-generation model (gptx-6b-fallback) with expected p95 increase to ~620ms.

Detailed notes from the run:
- Baseline p95 at 9,500 tps (avg prompt 600 tokens, seq_len=600): 360ms using int8 inference paths.
- With 4-bit (nf4) quantization we measured ~10-12% reduction in GPU memory (helpful for packing more concurrent contexts) but observed a ~6-10% latency increase on cold KV misses — p95 moves toward ~390–400ms in those windows.
- Nightly embedding batch (10M vectors): recommend a dedicated batch fleet: 2 x a2-batch instances scheduled in the 02:00–04:00 UTC slot. That meets the 2h window with a 10% compute buffer.

Attachments: capacity workbook includes sensitivity sheet (peaks at 10k/12k/14k tps) and the token->GPU mapping table.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to validate the SLA fallback language and burst minutes in the commercial SOW.
2) Rachel to run a tight p95 simulation for the marketing surge scenario with synthetic traces (we want to confirm cold-starts and KV-warmup assumptions).
3) If you confirm region split, we can allocate 1 slab (1 x rtx-c24-equivalent) to us-west and remainder to us-east to keep latency consistent for primary users.

[Attachment: redwood_stratacore_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (Excel, 170KB)]

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Linda Chen <linda.chen@stratacore.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Dec 2027 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet peaking profile + capacity ask for P1 launch

Quick notes from my side:
- Can we get the 5-minute time-series for the marketing surge (timestamps)? The sensitivity sheet assumes a square peak; if the peak is spiky we may need a slightly higher burst pool due to queueing.
- Confirming fallback model: gptx-6b-fallback will preserve basic UX but will reduce token cost by ~42% — useful for short bursts. Need to capture in SOW: fallback latency & quality expectations.
- On quantization: recommend we pilot nf4 only for the non-critical shards (read-heavy), keep int8 for primary low-latency endpoints unless the 4-bit profile gives you a pronounced cost saving.

I'll draft a short SLA paragraph for procurement around burst minutes and priority queuing.

—Ben
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Linda Chen <linda.chen@stratacore.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, ops+purchase@stratacore.com
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet peaking profile + capacity ask for P1 launch

Thanks — quick clarifications:
- Peak series attached (5-min resolution). The campaign launch pattern is more trapezoidal: ramp up ~8 mins, peak ~14 mins, ramp down ~10 mins.
- Region split: 70% US-East, 30% US-West for first 3 months.
- We want to avoid visible model downgrades for end-users; fallback is acceptable for delayed or non-critical completions. Can you quantify expected % of requests that will get fallback at 12k tps vs 14k tps? Procurement needs that.

[Attachment: marketing_peak_5min.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

-Linda

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Chen <linda.chen@stratacore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, ops+purchase@stratacore.com
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet peaking profile + capacity ask for P1 launch

Linda —

Thanks for the peak CSV. I re-ran the sensitivity with the trapezoidal shape and region split. Final recommended commercial numbers:

- Committed slab: 6 x rtx-c24-equivalent (maps to 9,500 tps steady-state). Region allocation: 4 slabs (us-east), 2 slabs (us-west).
- Burst policy (commercial): 35 minutes of burst allowance per day up to 12,000 tps, and an emergency credit-backed burst to 14,000 tps for up to 10 minutes/day (billing @ overage rate).
- Fallback exposure: at sustained 12,000 tps (your trapezoid peak) we estimate ~8–12% of requests will be queued into fallback model during the ~14-minute peak window. At 14,000 tps sustained, fallback exposure rises to ~28–33% during the central 10 minutes. These numbers assume KV cache warm starts and the hot-path batching we modeled.
- Latency expectations:
  - Primary path (int8, hot cache): p95 ~360–400ms during 12k bursts.
  - Fallback model p95: ~620–750ms.

Operational asks from us:
1) Sign-off on the burst minutes policy so procurement can encode into the SOW.
2) Confirmation of region split and whether you want the emergency credit for the 14k spike.
3) Rachel will run a real-trace simulation next week; expect a follow-up with a small delta to the fallback exposure numbers.

I'll prepare the commit recommendation PDF and a redlineable SLA paragraph for you and ops+purchase. If you want to tighten fallback exposure, next levers are: increase committed slabs to 8 (reduces fallback at 14k to ~12%), or schedule pre-warm cache windows before predicted launches (reduces cold-miss penalty).

[Attachment: commit_recommendation_summary.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
